summary.oneLiner: PVR INOX delivered record financials in FY26 with EBITDA margins doubling to 14.4% and net debt slashed 90% to INR161cr, driven by a decisive pivot to capital-light screen expansion (55% of new screens) and a structural boom in Indian box office (up 11% to INR13,519cr), making it the industry's dominant, cash-generative leader with a clear path to net cash.

one-line thesis: PVR INOX delivered record financials in FY26 with EBITDA margins doubling to 14.4% and net debt slashed 90% to INR161cr, driven by a decisive pivot to capital-light screen expansion (55% of new screens) and a structural boom in Indian box office (up 11% to INR13,519cr), making it the industry's dominant, cash-generative leader with a clear path to net cash.
financial scorecard: revenue: +16% YoY to INR6,742cr (IND AS 116); EBITDA/margin: +100% YoY to INR968cr, margin expanded from 8.4% to 14.4% (exceptional items excluded); PAT (rptd): INR386cr vs loss of INR152cr in FY25 (includes divestment gain from 4700BC); PAT (normalized): ~INR280cr (ex-divestment); order book: N/A; net debt: -90% YoY to INR161cr (negligible) - one-off: divestment gain of INR115cr in Q4 FY26 inflated PAT
guidance: revenue growth: implied 10-12% YoY (based on FY27 content slate); margin: sustained 14%+ EBITDA margin target; order inflow: 138 signed capital-light screens (52 FOCO, 86 asset-light); capex/commissioning: INR375-400cr in FY27 (INR225-250cr new screens, INR80-100cr renovations)
order book & pipeline: 138 signed capital-light screens (52 FOCO, 86 asset-light) to be commissioned over next 18 months
segment / subsidiary detail: Revenue mix: Box office (85%+), F&B (10%), Advertising (5%); Advertising growth slowed in FY26 due to delayed blockbuster releases (e.g., Jana Nayagan, Toxic); FOCO screens contribute management fee (10-14% of tenant revenue); Asset-light screens consolidate full P&L with developer capex contribution (40-80%)
growth verticals / optionality: Smart Cinema pilot (Tier 2/3) launching 2-3 screens by July 2026, targeting 28-30 screens this FY with 30-40% lower capex per screen; regional cinema expansion (Tamil, Telugu, Kannada); potential international licensing of brand
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded to 14.4% in FY26 due to revenue growth, cost discipline, and capital-light mix; rental cost as % of revenue expected to decline over 2-3 years as capital-light screens grow; F&B and advertising margins remain high
capex / expansion: FY26 capex: INR590cr; FY27 guidance: INR375-400cr (INR225-250cr new projects, INR80-100cr renovations, rest maintenance/IT); per-screen capex for Smart Cinema: 30-40% lower than mainstream
capital allocation: Net debt reduced to INR161cr; gross debt targeted for reduction to INR500cr; path to net cash in near term; dividend/buyback under Board review post net cash achievement
risks & watch-items: Macro consumption sensitivity (fuel prices, gold/tourism curbs); content delays; competition from OTT (though management deems this threat obsolete); execution risk in capital-light partnerships
management quality / tone: Highly confident, bullish on structural industry tailwinds (theatrical-first model), proud of balance sheet transformation, dismissive of macro headwinds, proactive on growth, optimistic on regional/Hollywood content
non-obvious takeaways: Management fee income from FOCO screens grew to INR13-14cr run rate (up from INR10cr in FY26) despite no capex - a hidden profit engine; Smart Cinema model is not just cost-reduction but a Tier 2/3 penetration play with 30-40% lower capex; ROU asset decline despite screen additions due to depreciation outpacing new lease additions

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

themes.title: Media, entertainment & out-of-home advertising
themes.need: Digital-content, music-IP licensing and an advertising-recovery cycle underpin media - TIPSMUSIC on music IP; ZEEL/ENIL/RADIOCITY/BTML on broadcast/content; HTMEDIA/DBCORP/HMVL on print + digital; SIGNPOST/BRIGHT-tier and UFO on OOH/cinema. Ad-spend revival is the near-term swing factor.
themes.driver: Festive ad-spend recovery; music-licensing/streaming monetization; OOH inventory uptake.
